title: Global error handling and standardised responses

videos.script: Ask the bookshop for a book that does not exist. It answers 404, and nothing else. No body, no reason. {{empty}} Send it a book with four mistakes in it. It answers 400 and a timestamp, and it does not say which four. {{vague}} Now send the same book twice. It takes both. {{duplicate}} An API is read by programs. A program cannot read your log, and it should not have to guess. It needs every error in one shape it can parse. {{shape}} This lesson gives the bookshop that shape. The service throws exceptions named in the shop's own words: book not found, duplicate ISBN. {{exceptions}} One class turns each of them into a problem document. That is the format RFC 9457 defines: a type, a title, a status and a detail. {{problem}} Spring's own errors come out in the same shape. A body that is not JSON. A path that does not exist. A method the path does not take. {{spring}} A failed validation lists every field that failed, and why. {{fields}} And an error nobody expected says nothing about the inside. No stack trace, no host name, no SQL. That goes to the log, where you can read it and a stranger cannot. {{leak}}
